key_insight: Replace costly optical-flow + warping pipelines with a state-space model (SSM) that treats video fusion as a sequential state update, enabling temporal fusion without explicit motion estimation.
problem_solved: Existing video fusion methods rely on optical flow and feature warping, which are computationally expensive and hard to scale for long sequences or real-time use.
method: Reformulate video fusion as a sequential state update process so temporal context is modeled as an evolving hidden state.
Use state-space models (SSMs) to capture long-range temporal dependencies efficiently, removing the need for optical flow estimation and feature warping.
Design an inference pipeline that updates and decodes the fusion state per frame, yielding lower compute and better scalability for longer videos.
impact: MambaVF reduces computation and latency for video fusion tasks, making high-quality temporal fusion practical for real-time systems and large-scale deployments without costly motion estimation.
